findings.finding: Unregistered bloat crossing that this diff deepens (limit 300). The Stop gate blocks on a TOUCHED file whose crossing is not in the baseline, and Group H1 reads it post-merge as a hook bypass. The crossing pre-exists this diff (301 before), but touching it arms the gate.

The load-bearing asymmetry - filter the REPO side, never the cache side - had zero test coverage. Both branches carry the same predicate, making the DRY hoist into walk_tracked_files the obvious refactor; that would blind the cache side permanently while every existing test stayed green.

sys.path.insert(0, scripts) contradicts the convention stated twice for this exact directory (append, not prepend - ADR-045 lib-collision one directory over), and drops the idempotence guard the siblings use.

The stated reason for not asserting the reverse direction was FALSE. 'Present on both sides' is not 'identical on both sides': diffs iterates repo hashes, so a filtered name can never be a diff and lands in cache_only, which sets no state and does not fail --strict. An over-broad entry therefore downgrades real content drift from blocking to advisory.

The assertion scanned the WHOLE shell file while its docstring scoped the rule to copy blocks. A future -not -name in a PRUNE block would demand that name in NOT_DISTRIBUTED - producing exactly the over-broad entry the finding above describes.

A new route to a zero-file green: if the filter ever empties a non-empty listing, tracked_count is 0 and state is ok - the 'a zero must never read as agreement' failure this module guards against twice elsewhere. Unreachable today, live the moment a broader entry joins.
'still shows as cache_only and gets pruned' promised a consequence the code does not deliver: cache_only sets no state, so --strict exits 0 and nothing compels a re-sync.
repo_tracked_files' docstring reasoned only about the COUNTED-not-dropped rule while the function now silently drops a third category.

The two-list pin covers only literal -name exclusions; *-globs and -not -path exclusions are unasserted prose claims about SKIP_SUFFIXES/SKIP_DIRS. Holds today; a future -not -name '*.log' or -not -path '*/docs/*' would reintroduce the bug undetected.
